smoke.notes: Honest negative, and the failure is the design working: test_manifest_exists_and_matches FAILED because the tracked tree drifted AFTER the import-baseline manifest was sealed (new receipts/exp013-curriculum*, exp012-root-replication* files are not in the sealed digest set) — the pin caught the drift loudly and names the fix (regenerate via tools/import_manifest.py, never edit by hand). All cell-mapping and collapse-ledger pins pass: id re-derivation, tamper naming, live re-execution of sealed receipts, Bell check.

essence: Smallest quantum framework taught to keep receipts: circuit = hash-chained cell ledger.

ideas.name: The smallest quantum framework
ideas.statement: MicroMoth (a maintained MicroQiskit fork) is pure stdlib Python readable in an afternoon; a zero-dependency JavaScript port plus a quantum-wow plugin bring click-and-play quantum randomness to any web page, degrading honestly from real hardware to simulation.

ideas.name: A circuit is already a ledger
ideas.statement: QuantumCircuit.data IS a cell chain: every gate a fnv1a-64-chained BIND cell, moments are TICK cells, and sugar ops decompose at append time so the chain never contains them — edit one gate and every downstream id moves.

ideas.name: Collapse is an event, not a state
ideas.statement: Seeded per-shot outcomes are EFFECT cells ({shot, outcome, seed}) that never mutate gate cells; each simulate() view is a receipted VIEW cell; an unseeded run is refused a seal — a collapse receipt is a re-executable claim, not a histogram number.

ideas.name: Sealed provenance and pins
ideas.statement: The import baseline (sha256 per tracked file) is sealed and pinned by tests that re-run the Bell check on every invocation; the fork is self-governing (upstream 404'd) with claims tagged VERIFIED vs RECORDED; the quantum-ops-as-cells premise is coordinated with quilt-qcells via a sibling-port gate, not duplicated.

parts.name: MicroMoth statevector core
parts.essence: The template micromoth.py (289 lines, stdlib only): QuantumCircuit with h/x/rx/rz/cx/crx/swap + decomposed y/z/ry, simulate() with counts/memory/probability_dictionary/statevector views; ports in Lua/C#/JS/Arduino.
parts.gate: Upstream tree untouched — the fleet adds only receipts around it
parts.failure_mode: Editing the baseline would break every sha256 pin downstream

parts.name: Circuit-as-ledger identity
parts.essence: One QuantumCircuit.data list IS a cell ledger — the ordered gate list already has the shape of an append-only chain ending in measurement events.
outputs: a hash-chained cell interpretation of the circuit
parts.failure_mode: Any out-of-band mutation of qc.data would desync ledger from circuit

parts.name: BIND/LINK gate chaining
parts.essence: Every gate application becomes a BIND cell {kind:'gate', args:{op, qubits, theta?}}; first gate's prev is genesis 0x0, later prevs are fnv1a-64 of the preceding cell; one explicit LINK per circuit boundary (simulator version, shots plan).
parts.gate: Edit one gate and every downstream id moves — the tamper-evidence property
parts.failure_mode: Silent gate edits are caught by id re-derivation in the pins

parts.name: Primitives, not sugar
parts.essence: y/z/ry decompose into rx/rz/x at append time (micromoth.py methods), so a circuit cell chain never contains them; the wrapper keeps a SUGAR set whose presence in qc.data would mean a hand-built, unbaseline chain.
parts.gate: Sugar ops in a chain are a refuse condition (sugar never ledgers)
parts.failure_mode: Non-canonical chains would be unverifiable against the baseline

parts.name: Collapse as EFFECT cells
parts.essence: Each shot outcome is an EFFECT cell {kind:'collapse', shot:i, outcome:bitstring, seed}; noise_model entries are EFFECT parameters, not silent edits — measurement is an event, never a mutation of gate cells.
parts.gate: A collapse event must never alter the gate chain
parts.failure_mode: Conflating measurement with mutation would destroy replayability

parts.name: VIEW cells over the same chain
parts.essence: simulate(qc, shots, get=...) is literally a VIEW cell {args:{shots,get}}; counts, statevector and probabilities_dict are three views of the SAME circuit chain — 'we looked at counts' is itself receipted and re-derivable.
parts.failure_mode: Unreceipted views would make analysis claims unreplayable

parts.name: TICK: moments as layers
parts.essence: The gate chain partitions into qubit-disjoint layers; a TICK cell closes each moment; depth = number of TICKs — coarse-grained time without touching gate order.
parts.failure_mode: Reordering gates within a moment would invalidate the depth claim

parts.name: Seal policy for collapse runs
parts.essence: simulate() takes NO seed argument and reads module-global random — the wrapper plumbs a seed through exactly that source (seed -> simulate -> restore), records the plumbing as the EFFECT parameter, and REFUSES to call an unseeded run sealed.
parts.gate: No seed plumbed and recorded => no seal
parts.failure_mode: Sealing an unseeded run would produce a collapse receipt nobody can re-execute

parts.name: Sibling-port gate
parts.essence: quilt-qcells (wave 49) claimed quantum-ops-as-cells for the engine itself; this lane coordinates rather than duplicates — the roadmap marks the quilt-native plugin as gated on that sibling.
parts.gate: No quilt-native code lands in this repo until the sibling-port question is settled
parts.failure_mode: Duplicate implementations would fork the cell algebra

parts.name: Import manifest tool
parts.essence: tools/import_manifest.py computes fnv1a-64 + sha256 per tracked file (267 files sealed), excludes itself by name and records the exclusion; receipts/import-baseline.json is regenerable and pinned.
parts.gate: The tool must exclude itself by name — self-reference would make the manifest unverifiable
parts.failure_mode: Observed live: the manifest now lags the tree (exp012/exp013 receipts added post-seal) and the pin FAILS loudly

parts.name: quantum-wow plugin with honest degrade
parts.essence: quantumSeed/quantumCoin/quantumField run simulated (default, no key) via a JS MicroMoth port; BYO-key real mode calls comet-qrng-v1 and DEGRADES gracefully back to simulated on any failure, always returning {mode, degraded, error}; CORS absence and zero-extractable-bytes NIST outcomes are receipted as honest limits.
outputs: seeds, coin flips, value fields + honesty metadata
parts.gate: Every public method returns a usable result plus mode/degraded — the widget must say what actually happened
parts.failure_mode: A silent fallback would fake IBM-hardware randomness

parts.name: Pins that re-derive and re-execute
parts.essence: test_collapse_ledger re-derives every cell id, names tamper locations, and LIVE re-executes sealed receipts; test_cell_mapping pins the doc's op table == simulate() dispatch; test_import_baseline re-runs the Bell check on every invocation — the import can never silently rot.
outputs: pass/fail with named tamper or drift
parts.gate: Pins must fail loudly and name the fix (regenerate the manifest, never edit by hand)
parts.failure_mode: 19/20 green today; the 1 failure is the manifest-drift pin doing exactly its job

parts.name: Provenance honesty tags
parts.essence: The declared upstream moth-quantum/MicroMoth returned 404 at import time, so the fork is self-governing: AUDIT.md's sealed baseline is the authority and every claim is tagged VERIFIED (run, dated) or RECORDED (read from repo metadata).
parts.gate: Nothing may be tagged VERIFIED without a run and a date
parts.failure_mode: Unverified claims would masquerade as checked facts

cells.expr: the gate list — identical object viewed as a cell chain
gate -> BIND cell, prev = fnv1a64(prev cell), genesis 0x0
y/z/ry decomposed at append; SUGAR in chain => refuse
simulate(get=...) recorded as a VIEW cell
qubit-disjoint moment partition; depth = TICK count
unseeded run => no SEALED status, ever
sha256 per tracked file, self-excluding tool
simulated default; BYO-key real comet-qrng-v1 with honest degrade
pytest pins: id re-derivation, tamper naming, live re-execution, Bell check

layer_logic.0: Substrate: a frozen stdlib statevector simulator whose ordered gate list is re-read as an append-only hash-chained ledger — nothing new inside the simulator, everything in the reading.
layer_logic.1: Mechanisms: BIND/LINK chaining of gates, sugar decomposition at append, EFFECT collapse events, VIEW receipts, TICK moment layers — five opcodes cover the whole circuit lifecycle.
layer_logic.2: Policy: no seal without a plumbed seed, no sugar in chains, and a sibling-port gate that refuses duplicate quantum-ops-as-cells work already claimed by quilt-qcells.
layer_logic.3: Interfaces: the self-excluding manifest tool, the pytest pin suite, and the quantum-wow web plugin whose every answer carries mode/degraded honesty metadata.
layer_logic.4: Evidence: sealed import baseline with VERIFIED/RECORDED tags, tamper-naming id re-derivation, live re-execution of collapse receipts — and today a loud, correct manifest-drift failure.
